cards.text: Pharaoh, king of Egypt, still won’t let Israel go. The LORD said one more plague was coming, and the Israelites did just what He commanded for the Passover (Exodus 11:1, 10; 12:28). Now it’s midnight.

cards.question: At midnight the LORD strikes the land of Egypt. Who does He strike down?
The plague reaches from Pharaoh’s own firstborn down to the firstborn of the prisoner in the dungeon, but the livestock are spared.

cards.text: In the night, Pharaoh gets up. So do all his officials and all the Egyptians.

cards.question: Loud wailing goes up across Egypt that night. Why is it everywhere?

answers.text: No house is without someone dead
Every field is burned to the ground
Every well in the land is dry

cards.text: Then Pharaoh summons Moses, Israel’s leader, and his brother Aaron (Exodus 4:14). In the middle of the night.

cards.question: Pharaoh has Moses and Aaron in front of him in the night. What does he tell them?

answers.text: Get up and leave my people
Worship your God here in Egypt

cards.question: Pharaoh tells Moses and Aaron to take their flocks and herds too. Then he asks them to bless him as well.

cards.text: And the Egyptians? They’re not just opening the door for Israel. They’re pushing them through it.

cards.question: The Egyptians urge Israel to hurry out of the land. Otherwise, they say, they are all going to ___.

cards.text: It’s all moving so fast, the people grab their dough before it’s leavened. Baker, I have RUSHED a batch before, but I have never grabbed the dough and RUN like it’s a fire drill.

cards.question: How do the people carry their unleavened dough out of Egypt?

answers.text: In kneading bowls on their shoulders
In clay jars on their donkeys
In baskets loaded on their carts

cards.text: The Israelites do one more thing, just like Moses told them. They go to the Egyptians and ask.

cards.question: The Israelites ask the Egyptians for articles of silver and gold, and for ___.
The Egyptians turn the Israelites down and send them off with nothing.

cards.text: The LORD gives the people such favor with the Egyptians that they grant the request, and in this way “they plundered the Egyptians.” That’s like asking the one coworker who NEVER shares for a chocolate chip, and they just hand it right over.
And they’re off! The Israelites set out from Rameses.

cards.question: The Israelites have left Rameses behind. Where does the journey take them?

cards.text: And this is not a small group, friend. I shared a drawer with a twist tie and a pile of rubber bands, and I thought THAT was crowded.

cards.question: About how many Israelite men are on foot, not counting the women and children?

cards.text: Animals are on the move too. Great droves of flocks and herds go up with them.

cards.question: Everyone who leaves Egypt with the Israelites is an Israelite.

cards.text: Out on the road, the people bake the dough they carried out of Egypt, with no kitchen and no counter. Baker to baker, I RESPECT that.

cards.question: The people bake the dough they carried out of Egypt into loaves made with leaven.
The Israelites hadn’t prepared any provisions for the trip. Why not?

answers.text: They were driven out and couldn’t delay
They thought Egypt would send supplies
Moses told them to travel light

cards.text: Now the Bible pauses the road trip to tell us how long Israel stayed in Egypt. And friend… I thought my years in the back of a junk drawer felt long.

cards.question: The Israelites’ stay in Egypt lasted ___ years.
All the LORD’s divisions go out of Egypt at the end of the 430 years, to the very day.

cards.text: That night, the LORD kept a vigil to bring them out of the land of Egypt.

cards.question: The LORD kept a vigil that night to bring Israel out of Egypt. Who is to keep that same night as a vigil to the LORD?

answers.text: All the Israelites for generations to come
Only the priests and Levites each year
Only Moses and Aaron that first year

cards.text: Then the LORD gives Moses and Aaron the statute of the Passover: who may eat it and how. A foreigner living among them can join once all the males in his household are circumcised, the meat stays inside one house, and none of the bones may be broken.

cards.question: After the LORD gives Moses and Aaron the Passover rules, the Israelites do just as He commanded.

cards.text: And on that very day, the LORD brings the Israelites out of the land of Egypt by their divisions. Friend, I know a little something about being brought out. But Israel’s road out of Egypt? It’s only getting started.

findings.problem: The setup says only that the Israelites ask the Egyptians; nothing in the earlier cards points to clothing rather than weapons or chariots. The blank therefore tests an unrevealed detail that the baker cannot reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The preceding card announces that the length of Israel's stay is coming, but gives no basis for choosing 430 over 40 or 70. This blank can be answered only by prior knowledge or luck.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three full sentences plus a question fragment, exceeding the limit of one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
